focus: What layout, spacing, grouping, connector-routing, density and section behaviour do the 22-repo corpus and Figma's own published skills demonstrate that a Mermaid model or the generator can steer?
answeredQuestions: What layout, spacing, grouping, connector-routing, density and section behaviour do the 22-repo corpus and Figma's own published skills demonstrate that a Mermaid model or the generator can steer?

label: Figma's own board skill states a board reading order - left to right, top to bottom, context on the left, evidence in the middle, proposal and asks on the right, supporting detail and appendix below - and sk-create-figjam has no statement about how a reader traverses the finished board.

Figma states the board's spacing language as three named distances - tight clustering 60-92px is the same thought, loose 200-400px is a different topic, zone breaks 1000px+ are a different part of the board - which is an order of magnitude larger than the comparator's 24px node gap, so the packet cannot adopt diagram-side spacing and should adopt this board-side scale instead.

Figma requires every board to have an entry point - a 60-96px board title top-left, visible at overview zoom, plus a meta or agenda element - while the packet's title recipe matches the position but not the scale (a default text node is a label, not a 60-96px title) and is gated as an optional extension.

Sections nest on a FigJam board by design - a board is a section containing zone sections containing card sections - so the packet's rule that a section never wraps a generated node is a policy protecting generated geometry from appendChild's parent-relative coordinates, not a platform limit; sectioning remains possible if the geometry is not moved.

Figma's own diagram skill says the fix for a cramped or tangled generated diagram is better Mermaid, not manual repositioning via use_figma - which independently confirms the packet's layer choice and identifies the missing artifact exactly: nobody says what better Mermaid is, and that is the only lever the generator leaves.

Figma treats a title block and a side legend as ordinary extension work that needs no board inspection, where the packet routes every extension through a request-driven gate, so the two skills hold opposite default postures and Figma's is the one that produces a board a stranger can read.

The corpus formalises glance order as three lines written before placing nodes - first glance wins within two seconds, second glance advances the argument, last glance stays available without competing - and warns that repeating the primary claim in a title and a hero card creates two focal objects for one idea; the packet has one accent rule at node level and nothing at board level.

The corpus states a focus budget per section - one primary focal object, two or three secondary, everything else quieter through scale, contrast, container or position, with position and visual mass before typography and colour last - which is the packet's one-accent rule scoped to a board, minus the de-emphasis half that does the actual work.

The corpus gives spacing a semantic scale keyed to relationship - 16-32px inside a text stack, 32-48px card padding, 60-92px between peer objects, 160-240px between distinct groups - and the operative rule that unrelated groups should never be closer than the text blocks inside a card; the packet's only grouping affordance is a tint at a 24px constant, where the corpus asks for a ratio between within-group and between-group distance.

The corpus makes text size computable from viewing distance - reviewScale = min(1, 1200/max(w,h)), rendered targets of 44-56px title, 32-44px section heading, 13-18px body and 10-13px metadata at that overview, and viewing distance overrides the nominal preset - which turns the packet's missing size dial into something an extension can compute and a reviewer can check.

The corpus supplies the two-pass review the scorecard lacks: an overview zoom that identifies what actually wins first, second and last and revises scale, position, contrast or grouping when the order differs from the plan, then a reading zoom for line length, wraps, breathing room, connector labels and clipping, with the verdict that a structurally valid board can still be compositionally unresolved.

The corpus's geometry audit gives the collision tests a board review can run - at least 12px and preferably 16-32px between vertically consecutive overlapping text blocks, every non-connector child checked against its parent bounds, and connector crossings judged from the rendered screenshot because a bounding box does not describe a path - which is exactly the judgment the packet's position-blind read-back cannot make.

Figma's own sticky geometry contradicts the packet's legend column: stickies are fixed at 240x240 or 416x240 and must be laid out in a grid on a 64px gap, while the packet stacks legend stickies in one column at a 32px gap, half the platform rhythm, which is why the legend reads as a list rather than a FigJam object.

The packet already matches or beats Figma's own guidance where content is constrained - a 40-character label cap, a per-type node budget and a named shape vocabulary per type, where Figma states no label cap, no budget and only distinct fills per node type - so the corpus adds layout and measurement vocabulary but no content discipline the packet lacks.

direction: Adopt the corpus 1200px overview normalisation as a literal board rule
reason: It assumes a wrapper the packet does not own; the transferable part is the review-scale method, not the constant.

direction: Use the Mermaid importer repos as design sources
reason: Read and dismissed: they document import mechanics and state no composition or legibility rule.

direction: Treat Figma's board-content skill as a competitor to sk-create-figjam
reason: It explicitly routes flowcharts, architecture, sequence, state and ER to generate_diagram, so it is the board layer the packet lacks.
